sentences.text:
2. Heard the learned Counsel for the parties.
3.

On the complaint of Smt. Venkataravanamma W/o Srinivasa dated 09.04.2021, Bagepalli police have registered FIR in Crime No.91/2021 against the petitioner for the offence punishable under Section 363 IPC.
4.
In the complaint, it is averred that complainant's second daughter was studying in 10th Standard and she was born on NC: 2023:KHC:29190 14.02.2005.
On 09.04.2021, complainant's minor daughter had gone out from the house.
However, thereafter she had not returned.
Complainant's husband made efforts to search her, but the same was in vain.

Complainant suspected the hand of the petitioner, and therefore, had lodged a complaint which had resulted in registering FIR in Crime No.91/2021.
5.
During the course of investigation, petitioner was arrested on 10.08.2021.
Investigation in the case is completed and charge sheet has been filed.
Petitioner's bail application filed before the Trial Court in Crl.Misc.No.814/2022 was dismissed on 30.12.2022.

It is under these circumstances,

6. Learned Counsel for the petitioner has reiterated the grounds urged in the petition and submits that the victim girl and her mother have been examined before the Trial Court.
Investigation in the case is completed and material witnesses have been examined.
Therefore, petitioner is not required in custody.
He submits that the petitioner has been falsely implicated in the case.
The medical records do not support the case of the prosecution, and therefore, he prays to allow the petition.

Per contra, learned HCGP has opposed the bail application and submits that PWs-1 & 2 have supported the case of the prosecution, and therefore, there is a prima facie case against the petitioner for the alleged offence.
Accordingly, she prays to dismiss the petition.

8. The defacto complainant who is the mother of the victim girl has been examined as PW-1 before the Trial Court and the victim girl who was aged about 16 years as on the date of the incident has been examined as PW-2.
Both the witnesses have fully supported the case of the prosecution.
The victim girl has stated that the petitioner had forcibly taken her to his house and confined her in the said house.
She has stated that after she was taken to the house, she came to know that the petitioner was already married.
The petitioner had kept the minor girl in his house for a period of three months and had committed repeated sexual assault on her against her wish.
Petitioner has been charge sheeted for the heinous offence punishable under 363, 376(2)(n) of IPC and Sections 4 & 6 of POCSO Act.
The material witnesses who have been examined before the Trial Court have fully supported the case of the prosecution.

The doctor who has issued the medical report is NC:
2023:KHC:29190 yet to be examined before the Trial Court.

Considering the material available on record, more so the evidence of PWs-1 & 2, it cannot be said that there is no material as against the petitioner for the offences for which he has been charge sheeted.
Under the circumstances, I am of the view that the petitioner has not made out a prima facie case for grant of regular bail.
Accordingly, the petition is dismissed.
